chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Munthir ibn Yazid who said: Abu Harun al-Makfuf narrated to me

He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Harun! Indeed God the Blessed and Exalted has sworn by Himself not to be a neighbor to a treacherous one.' I asked: 'Who is the treacherous one?' He said: 'One who saves for himself a dirham of a believer's money or withholds from him anything of worldly affairs.' I said: 'I seek refuge in God from God's wrath.' Then he said: 'Indeed God the Blessed and Exalted has sworn by Himself not to house in His Paradise three types: one who rejects God's judgment, or one who rejects the judgment of a righteous Imam, or one who withholds the right of a believer.' I asked: 'Should he give him from the surplus of what he owns?' He said: 'He should give him from his own self and soul.' If a Muslim is stingy with his own self towards him, he is not of him; rather he is of the progeny of Satan.' The compiler of this book (may God increase his support) said: 'Giving from the self and soul means offering one's status/effort to him when he needs assistance, and striving for him in his needs.'

key_terms.أَدَّخَرَ: To save up / hoard for oneself
key_terms.يُجَاوِرَهُ: To be a neighbor to / dwell near

ai.seo_question: Who is considered a 'treacherous' person in Shia hadith regarding the rights of believers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the concept of *Al-Lahu al-Lahu* (God’s self-sworn oath) to emphasize the severity of withholding a believer's rights, defining treachery not merely as deceit but as the retention of even a single dirham or essential worldly need. The narration expands the definition of generosity (*I'ti'*) beyond material surplus to include self-sacrifice and active advocacy for one's needs, framing stinginess as a form of *Shirk al-Shaytan* (Satanic polytheism) due to the hoarding of self for oneself.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-185 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Sahl ibn Zyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Zayd , on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Monzar ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Makfoof,

“Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) told me, ‘O Aba Harun! Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God has sworn by Himself not to be neighbors with treacherous ones.’ I asked, ‘Who would that refer to?’ the Imam (MGB) replied, ‘That refers to anyone who takes even a penny of a believer’s money for himself or deprives him of worldly things.’ I said, ‘I seek refuge in God from God’s Wrath!’ Then the Imam (MGB) added, ‘Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God has sworn by Himself not to house any of the following three groups in Paradise: those who reject God’s judgement; those who reject the judgement of a righteous Divine Leader, and those who disregard a believer’s rights.’ I asked, ‘Should one give a believer what he has a lot more of than his own needs?’ The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘One should not hesitate to do anything for him. Should he hesitate to give him his own self and soul, he is not of his brethren. Rather he would be of the progeny of Satan.’”The compiler of the book - may God increase his acknowledgement - said, “What is meant here by not hesitating to give from one’s self and soul is to assist him whenever he needs any assistance and to help him to fulfill his needs.”
